paleo.label: Paleontologist
paleo.text: Each one earns 5 research points a day and runs one research bay, one project at a time.

temporal.label: Temporal Researcher
temporal.text: Each one runs an expedition bay with one team. More researchers means more trips at the same time.

gene.label: Geneticist
gene.text: Each one runs an incubator bay, so TAR can grow that many clones at the same time.

botanist.label: Botanist
botanist.text: Each one tends a growing bed, so CERES can grow that many batches at the same time.

oracle.label: ORACLE
oracle.full: Operational Requests for Ancestral & Chronological Life Evidence
oracle.blurb: The research hub. Unlocks animals, plants, medicine, fences, buildings, and TAR upgrades. Research takes time.

ghost.label: GHOST
ghost.full: Genetic Harvesting of Organic Specimens through Time
ghost.blurb: The time travel unit. Sends teams to the periods of animals ORACLE has unlocked, and fills their genomes with DNA.

tar.label: TAR
tar.blurb: The cloning lab. Turns complete genomes into living animals.

station.label: Keeper Station
station.blurb: Keepers start here and hold a small stock of food. Zone hubs: custodians restock them from bigger stores.

breakroom.label: Break Room
breakroom.blurb: Tired keepers rest here four times faster than at a station.

toolshed.label: Tool Shed
toolshed.blurb: Buy upgrades that make keepers' and custodians' work easier.

security.label: Security Office
security.blurb: Guards start here. They patrol the paths, put rowdy guests off, throw out vandals, and steer guests to the gate during escapes.

closet.label: Custodial Closet
closet.blurb: Custodians start here. They restock food stands and gift shops, scrub restrooms, empty bins, and sweep litter.

workshop.label: Workshop
workshop.blurb: Mechanics are based here. They inspect and repair exhibit barriers.

ceres.label: CERES
ceres.blurb: The greenhouse lab. Grows Paleoflora food for prehistoric plant-eaters, plants for exhibits, and medicine for the PMC, once ORACLE has unlocked them and GHOST has found the plant DNA. Keepers collect Paleoflora here.

greenhouse.label: Greenhouse
greenhouse.blurb: Adds 40 units of Paleoflora a day to CERES.

generator.label: Generator
generator.blurb: Powers every electrified fence in the park. Mechanics keep it running.

depot.label: Vehicle Depot
depot.blurb: Adds 3 ATVs for staff to share. They drive five times faster than walking, but only on service roads, and an ATV stays where it was left. Mechanics keep it running.

warehouse.label: Warehouse
warehouse.blurb: Stores hay, insect feed, drinks, and merchandise, and keeps them better than a station does. Custodians restock stations, stands and shops from here.

coldstore.label: Cold Store
coldstore.blurb: Keeps meat, fish, medicine, and snacks from rotting, as long as it has power from a generator.

dock.label: Delivery Dock
dock.blurb: Order animal food and stock for your stands and shops. Trucks come overnight and every two hours while the park is open. They need a service road to the entrance. Keepers and custodians carry it from here.

farm.label: Hay Farm
farm.blurb: Grows 60 units of hay a day.

ranch.label: Livestock Ranch
ranch.blurb: Raises 40 units of meat a day. Meat spoils fast, so keep a cold store nearby.

hatchery.label: Fish Hatchery
hatchery.blurb: Breeds 40 units of fish a day. It spoils fastest of all.

insectary.label: Insectary
insectary.blurb: Breeds 30 units of insects a day.

pmc.label: Paleo-Medicine Center
pmc.blurb: Vets are based here. They give exhibits routine check-ups, treat minor illnesses on the spot, dart serious cases and escaped animals, and treat patients with medicine from CERES.

map.label: Park maps
map.text: Guests with a map don't mind long walks.

umbrella.label: Umbrellas
umbrella.text: Sells far better when it rains.

paleobook.label: Paleontology books
paleobook.text: Guests who read one learn more, and learn more at every exhibit after.

noFood.text: I'm hungry and there's nowhere to eat.

noDrink.text: I'm thirsty and there's nothing to drink.

accident.text: I couldn't find a restroom in time.

queue.text: The queue was so long I gave up.

far.text: Everything is such a long walk.

pacing.text: The animals just paced back and forth.

scared.text: An animal got loose. We're getting out of here!

pricey.text: The ticket cost far too much.

noSeat.text: My feet hurt and there's nowhere to sit.

litter.text: There's trash all over the paths.

priceyFood.text: The food here costs too much.

rested.text: It was nice to sit down for a bit.

soldOut.text: They'd sold out of what I wanted.

broken.text: The benches here are all broken.

safe.text: Seeing guards around made me feel safe.

noInfo.text: I wish there were signs telling us about the animals.

priceyEdu.text: The Education Center costs too much to get in.

learned.text: I learned so much about prehistoric life!

UPGRADES.label: Shovels
UPGRADES.text: Keepers clean exhibits 2.5 times faster than with bare hands.

UPGRADES.label: Hoses
UPGRADES.text: Keepers clean exhibits another 2.5 times faster.

UPGRADES.label: Wheelbarrows
UPGRADES.text: Keepers carry 2.5 times as much food per trip.

UPGRADES.label: Work boots
UPGRADES.text: Keepers tire 40% more slowly while walking.

UPGRADES.label: Cooler boxes
UPGRADES.text: Food spoils 40% more slowly in every store.

UPGRADES.label: Pallet forklift
UPGRADES.text: Custodians restocking stores carry 3 times as much per trip.

UPGRADES.label: Litter pickers
UPGRADES.text: Custodians sweep litter twice as fast.

UPGRADES.label: Janitor carts
UPGRADES.text: Custodians carry twice as much stock per trip.

UPGRADES.label: Pressure washers
UPGRADES.text: Custodians scrub restrooms twice as fast.

paleozoic.label: Paleozoic
paleozoic.plants: lycopod trees, horsetails, and seed ferns

TECH.label: Metal bars
TECH.text: Strength 45. Holds mid-size herbivores.

TECH.label: Electrified fence
TECH.text: Strength 65 while powered. Holds most herbivores and smaller predators. Needs generators.

TECH.label: Concrete walls
TECH.text: Strength 140. Holds anything, but guests can barely see in.

TECH.label: Acrylic walls
TECH.text: Strength 85. Clear walls that guests love looking through.

TECH.label: Aviary netting
TECH.text: Carbon fiber and steel mesh over an exhibit, so flying animals can't escape.

TECH.label: Catch netting
TECH.text: Netting along an exhibit's fence that catches 95% of the trash guests throw in. It catches less as the fence wears.

TECH.label: Moats
TECH.text: Stops every escape from an exhibit, whatever its walls.

TECH.label: Viewing platforms
TECH.text: Raised decks on an exhibit's edge. Guests enjoy the exhibit far more.

TECH.label: Education programs
TECH.text: Build an Education Center, where guests learn about prehistoric life. Educated guests are happier, tidier, and more generous.

TECH.label: Modern design
TECH.text: Unlocks the Modern theme: polished stone, metal and glass for paths, buildings and exhibits.

TECH.label: Hotels
TECH.text: Build campgrounds, safari lodges, and resort hotels. Guests stay the night and spend the next day in the park.

TECH.label: Cold stores
TECH.text: Refrigerated stores that keep meat, fish, medicine, and snacks from rotting. Needs power.

TECH.label: Security offices
TECH.text: Build a Security Office and hire guards to patrol, deter vandals, and steer guests out during escapes.

TECH.label: Power generators
TECH.text: Diesel generators that power electrified fences and cold stores.

TECH.label: Security cameras
TECH.text: Each Security Office watches the paths around it, and you can put camera posts on paths to watch more. Guards are sent straight to vandals the cameras see.

TECH.label: Staff vehicles
TECH.text: Vehicle depots with ATVs. Staff drive five times faster, but only on service roads.

TECH.label: Guest tram
TECH.text: Draw tram track and build tram stations beside it. Guests ride between stations instead of walking, and pay a fare.

TECH.label: Food production
TECH.text: Build farms, ranches, hatcheries, and insectaries to make animal food. Cheaper than the dock, but it spoils if nobody collects it.

TECH.label: Faster incubators
TECH.text: Clones finish in three quarters of the time.

TECH.label: Much faster incubators
TECH.text: Clones finish in about half the time.

TECH.label: Leaner expeditions
TECH.text: Trips cost about a fifth less.

TECH.label: Lean expeditions
TECH.text: Trips cost about a third less.

TECH.label: Faster time engines
TECH.text: Expeditions take three quarters of the time.

TECH.label: Much faster time engines
TECH.text: Expeditions take about half the time.

TECH.label: Careful sampling
TECH.text: Every DNA sample comes back 8 points better in quality.

TECH.label: Cryo-preserved samples
TECH.text: Every DNA sample comes back 16 points better in quality.

TECH.label: Genome therapy
TECH.text: Vets can rewrite a sickly clone's DNA to match the lab's best genome for its species, making it healthier. Needs a Paleo-Medicine Center, and only goes as far as the lab's own DNA quality, so send GHOST for better samples to raise it.

TECH.label: Paleoflora cultivation
TECH.text: CERES starts growing Paleoflora, the food prehistoric plant-eaters need instead of grass. It needs plant DNA from GHOST first.

TECH.label: Mesozoic flora
TECH.text: Cycads, conifers, ginkgos, and ferns. Once researched, GHOST can collect each period's plant DNA, then CERES grows its plants for exhibits.

TECH.label: Paleozoic flora
TECH.text: Lycopod trees, horsetails, and seed ferns. Once researched, GHOST can collect each period's plant DNA, then CERES grows its plants for exhibits.

TECH.label: Sterile prehistoric plants
TECH.text: Seedless de-extinct plants that can't spread, so plants from any period can grow out in the park, along paths and in gardens. Mesozoic and Paleozoic ones still come from CERES.

TECH.label: Greenhouses
TECH.text: Build greenhouses near CERES to grow Paleoflora faster.

TECH.label: Cenozoic medicine
TECH.text: CERES grows medicine for Paleogene, Neogene, and Quaternary animals. Refine it for each period to cure them fully.

TECH.label: Mesozoic medicine
TECH.text: CERES grows medicine for Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous animals. Needs Mesozoic plant DNA. Refine it for each period to cure them fully.

TECH.label: Paleozoic medicine
TECH.text: CERES grows medicine for Devonian, Carboniferous and Permian animals. Needs Paleozoic plant DNA. Refine it for each period to cure them fully.

st-anning.label: Mary Anning
st-anning.text: Found the first ichthyosaur and plesiosaurs on the cliffs at Lyme Regis.

st-brown.label: Barnum Brown
st-brown.text: Dug up the first Tyrannosaurus rex.

st-marsh.label: O.C. Marsh
st-marsh.text: Named Stegosaurus, Triceratops and Apatosaurus in the Bone Wars.

st-cope.label: E.D. Cope
st-cope.text: Named over a thousand species, Dimetrodon among them, in the Bone Wars.

anning.label: Mary Anning
anning.text: Found the first ichthyosaur and plesiosaurs on the cliffs at Lyme Regis.

brown.label: Barnum Brown
brown.text: Dug up the first Tyrannosaurus rex.

marsh.label: O.C. Marsh
marsh.text: Named Stegosaurus, Triceratops and Apatosaurus in the Bone Wars.

cope.label: E.D. Cope
cope.text: Named over a thousand species, Dimetrodon among them, in the Bone Wars.

genesis.label: Genesis
genesis.blurb: A conservation campus: forest green metal roofs, pale lab membranes, poured concrete and matte gold trim. Practical, never ornate.

gilded.label: Gilded Age
gilded.blurb: Cobblestones, slate roofs, wrought iron and brass. 1800s paleontology, retro paleoart.

bayou.label: Bayou
bayou.blurb: Weathered boardwalks, tin roofs, cypress posts and still water.

volcanic.label: Volcanic
volcanic.blurb: Black basalt, steel and ash, with heat glowing through the cracks.

stone.label: Stone Age
stone.blurb: Frozen tundra, flagstones, stacked stone and lashed timber, thatch and hide. Cold and rough, with no paint anywhere.

unlock.hint: Earn the grant for cloning a Quaternary animal.

lodge.label: Nordic
lodge.blurb: Longhouses and stave churches in the snow: dark shingle roofs under blue-white drifts, turf-roofed huts, carved ridge tips, deep red trim and split-log rails. Warm, tidy and finished.

mesa.label: Mesa
mesa.blurb: Pueblo adobe, sandstone, cactus and turquoise in the Southwest desert.

modern.label: Modern
modern.blurb: Cool and light: green roofs, gray metal and glass skylights on pale concrete and mown grass, with dark wood for warmth and glass panel fences.

japanese.label: Japanese Garden
japanese.blurb: Calm and precise: curved tile roofs, golden thatch, dark timber walkways with pebble edges, bamboo lattice and plaster walls, clipped moss and raked gravel. Red is kept for lanterns.

tropical.label: Tropical
tropical.blurb: Lush and bright: thatch huts, bamboo and teak, pale stepping stones, big leaves and bursts of flowers. Tidy and cared for, unlike the Bayou.

unlock.hint: Keep an animal in a tropical exhibit.

roadside.label: Retro
roadside.blurb: 1960s highway attraction: cream and turquoise roofs with bold stripes, chrome trim, painted asphalt and pastel pipe rails, like a diner and a motor lodge that decided to have dinosaurs.

homestead.label: Homestead
homestead.blurb: Wyoming ranch country: wind-combed prairie, dirt roads, rusty tin barns and split-rail fences.

unlock.hint: Keep an animal in a grassland exhibit.

GOALS.hint: Open Build, then Exhibit Tools, pick a fence type, then tap corners on the map. Tap the first corner again to close it.

GOALS.text: Connect an exhibit to the path
GOALS.hint: Guests only see exhibits that touch a path from the entrance. Use Guest Paths under Path Tools to reach it.
Tap an exhibit, then buy starter animals from partner parks in the side panel.
Pick Food, then Cart, and tap next to a path. Tap the cart and choose what it sells. Hungry guests rate the park lower.
Guests need restrooms too. Place them next to a path.
Partner parks feed your animals until day 5. Before then, build a Keeper Station beside a path or service road, tap it, and hire a keeper.

Animal food has to be bought now. Build a Delivery Dock beside a service road. It orders overnight, custodians stock a station from it, and keepers carry the food out to the exhibits. Partner parks cover the first deliveries.

Stands and shops sell from their own stock, and someone has to carry it from the dock. Build a Custodial Closet beside a path or service road and hire a custodian. They also clean restrooms and sweep litter.
Unhappy, rowdy guests break benches and spray graffiti. Research Security offices at ORACLE, build one beside a path, and hire a guard to patrol. Lamp posts help too.

GOALS.text: Give an exhibit a Keeper Gate
GOALS.hint: Run a path or service road to an exhibit's fence, then use Gates under Exhibit Tools on that fence.
Fences wear down, and predators attack them. Build a Workshop beside a path or service road and hire a mechanic to inspect and repair them.
Animals get sick, and some get hurt fighting. Build a Paleo-Medicine Center beside a path or service road and hire a vet. Vets also dart escaped animals.
Zones split the park into areas with their own keepers and stores. Pick the Zone tool, draw around some exhibits and a station, then assign keepers to it from its panel.
More animals and happier animals bring more guests.
Keep adding animals, food, restrooms and room on the paths. Happy guests tell their friends.
Every other animal comes from the past. ORACLE researches time periods. Place it beside a path or service road.
Tap ORACLE and hire a paleontologist. They earn research points as the day goes on. Open the Cenozoic tab (Paleogene, Neogene, Quaternary) and start unlocking an animal.
Open the Mesozoic tab (Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous) at ORACLE and start unlocking an animal.
Open the Paleozoic tab (Devonian, Carboniferous, Permian) at ORACLE and start unlocking an animal.
Unlock and complete the genome of a Quaternary animal, then clone it at TAR.

GOALS.text: Build GHOST and send an expedition
GOALS.hint: GHOST travels to the periods of animals you've unlocked. Hire a Temporal Researcher at GHOST, then pick the animal under its period's tab and send GHOST.
Each sample fills part of a genome. Keep sending trips for the same species until it reaches 100%.

GOALS.text: Build TAR and clone an animal
GOALS.hint: TAR turns a complete genome into an animal. Hire a Geneticist at TAR, then order clones from TAR or from an exhibit's panel.
Medicine for prehistoric animals is grown at CERES, once ORACLE has researched it. Place it beside a path or service road and hire a botanist.
Variety raises your rating. Herbivores can share an exhibit.
Keep animals happy, give guests food and restrooms, and add variety.
Earn more than you spend. Check the day report after closing.
Unlock the Tyrannosaurus at ORACLE, collect a full T. rex genome with GHOST, and reach 4.5 stars. It needs a lot of room.
Research Hotels at ORACLE. Once your park has 2 stars and 100 guests a day, build a Campground beside a path. Guests stay the night and spend tomorrow in the park.
Once your park has 3 stars and 300 guests a day, build a Safari Lodge beside a path.
Once your park has 4 stars and 700 guests a day, build a Resort Hotel beside a path.
